Components of Google Chrome Browser

  • User Interface: This is the part of the browser that you interact with directly. It includes the toolbar, address bar, tabs, bookmarks bar, and more.
  • Rendering Engine: Rendering engine is the component that takes web page code (HTML, CSS, and JavaScript) and converts it into the pixels that you see on your screen. Chrome uses the Blink rendering engine, which is a fork of the WebKit engine used by Safari.
  • JavaScript Engine: Javascript engine is the component that executes JavaScript code on web pages. Chrome uses the V8 JavaScript engine, which is known for its speed and efficiency.
  • Networking Stack: This is the component that handles communication between Chrome and the internet. It includes features such as HTTP/2 support, proxy support, and security features like sandboxing.
  • Security Sandbox: Security feature that isolates each tab in its own process, so that a malicious website cannot harm other tabs or your computer.
  • Extensions: These are small programs that you can add to Chrome to add new features or functionality.
  • Themes: Visual customizations that you can apply to Chrome to change its appearance.
  • Settings: These allow you to control how Chrome works, such as its privacy settings, search engine, and startup behavior.

These are just the main components of Google Chrome. There are many other smaller components that work together to make the browser function.
